title: Phenol/Chloroform Genomic DNA Extraction from Tissue Culture Cells
author: John Tyson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7ejhjcn

steps.title: Harvest Cells
steps.instruction: Remove tissue culture media from two T25 flasks of cells (~ 1 x 10^7 cells per flask, or 60–80% confluency).

steps.title: Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Gently scrape the surface of the two T25 flasks with a cell scraper and pour the viscous sample into a 50 ml tube.

steps.title: Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells using lysis buffer and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL of Lysis buffer per flask.
Gently rock back and forth for ~ 00:01:00.
Incubate for 01:00:00 at 37 °C.

steps.title: Digest Proteins
steps.instruction: Add Proteinase K and incubate to digest proteins.

substeps.instruction: Add proteinase K (20mg/ml) to a final concentration of 100 μg/ml.
Incubate the lysate at 56 °C for 03:00:00, occasionally mixing by inversion.

steps.title: Phenol Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform phenol extraction to remove proteins.

substeps.instruction: Allow the sample to cool to Room temperature.
Add an equal volume of buffer-saturated phenol.
Gently mix by inversion for a few minutes until an emulsion is formed.
Centrifuge at 5000 x g for 00:30:00 – 01:00:00 at Room temperature to separate phases.
Use a wide-bore pipette to transfer the upper viscous aqueous phase to a fresh tube, avoiding the interface.

steps.title: Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform chloroform extraction to further purify the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of Chloroform.
Mix by gentle inversion for approximately one minute.
Centrifuge at 5000 x g for 00:30:00 at Room temperature to separate phases.
Use a wide-bore pipette to transfer the upper viscous aqueous phase to a fresh 50 ml tube, avoiding the interface.

steps.title: DNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the genomic DNA from the aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Add NaCl from a 5 Molarity (M) stock to increase the concentration by 0.3 Molarity (M).
Add 2 volumes of ethanol.
Mix by gentle inversion of the tube several times.
Mix by gentle inversion.
Mix by inversion a couple of times and then gentle swirling.
Let sit at Room temperature for ~ 00:30:00.

steps.title: Recover DNA Condensate
steps.instruction: Collect the precipitated DNA using a glass capillary.

substeps.instruction: Hook out the stringy mass of condensed DNA using a glass capillary with a hook made at the end.

steps.title: Wash DNA
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA condensate to remove residual salts.

substeps.instruction: Dip the DNA condensate into a series of three 1 ml tubes containing 70% ethanol, holding for ~ 00:00:20 in each.

steps.title: Dry and Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Dry the DNA and resuspend it in buffer.

substeps.instruction: Allow the DNA on the glass capillary to air-dry for ~ 00:01:00 (hold upside down to allow excess liquid to rundown and dab away with a tissue, avoiding the DNA).
Place the end of the glass capillary into a tube containing 100 µL – 200 µL Buffer EB (10 Molarity (M) Tris-Cl pH 8.0).
Gently dislodge the DNA from the glass capillary until no 'gel' mass remains on the capillary.

steps.title: Hydrate DNA
steps.instruction: Store the DNA to allow for full hydration.

substeps.instruction: Place the DNA solution in the fridge and leave for a few days to fully hydrate before use.
